title: Canonical coefficient comparisons intertwine derived exchange
statement: Let Λ : Type (u+1) be a commutative ring and let f:X→Y, f′:X′→Y′, g′:X′→X, g:Y′→Y be any commutative square of schemes. For each edge, fix the inverse-image coefficient comparison to be the mate of the forgotten module adjunction unit [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-inverse-image-comparison], and fix the derived direct-image comparison to be rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange of the evaluation identity [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison]. For any K in D⁺(Sheaf(X_et,ModuleCat Λ)), define s_K:DU_Y′(Dg_Mod Rf_Mod K)≅Dg_Ab Rf_Ab(DU_X K) by the inverse g comparison followed by Dg_Ab of the f comparison, and r_K:DU_Y′(Rf′_Mod Dg′_Mod K)≅Rf′_Ab Dg′_Ab(DU_X K) by the f′ comparison followed by Rf′_Ab of the inverse g′ comparison. Then DU_Y′(Ex_Mod(K)) followed by r_K equals s_K followed by Ex_Ab(DU_X K), for the canonical derivedBaseChangeMapPlus transformations [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. This is equality for fixed maps, not existence of comparison isomorphisms. No stalk or degree is involved.

proof.text: Use the canonical edge comparisons. Their construction fixes the comparison of direct-image derived units. The underived inverse-image comparison is the mate of the forgotten module unit, so the corresponding units and counits agree under it. Lift the exact inverse-image comparison using mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso and composition isomorphisms.

Expand the underived exchange as adjunction unit, commutation isomorphism for the square, and counit. Direct image and its composition identification commute with forgetting by evaluation. The mate identities from the first step make this precisely the abelian underived exchange, with the fixed edge comparisons.

For both derived transformations, precompose on every bounded below module complex with the forgotten g image of the f derived unit. Use rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_fac for the coefficient comparison and derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_fac_app for exchange. The preceding underived equality identifies both resulting transformations; exact-functor factorization isomorphisms and naturality transport the terms. Uniqueness of the right derived transformation gives the stated equality for all K. This avoids an assumption that forgetting preserves injectives.
